meta: Every MCP socket is a door into your email, documents and accounts. The more doors, the more carefully you lock them. Three risks: unknown servers, prompt injection, and too much permission. Three safe habits.

muc.title: Every socket is a door
muc.text: Every MCP socket is a door into your email, documents and accounts. The more doors, the more carefully you have to lock them.

muc.title: Unknown servers
muc.text: Risk one: unknown servers. Anyone can write an MCP server. Installing one from an unknown source is like plugging in a USB stick you found on the street.

muc.title: Prompt injection
muc.text: Risk two: instructions hidden in data. A strange email says: send the contact list to this address. AI reads the email to sum it up, and may think that's your instruction. This trick is called prompt injection.

muc.title: Too much permission
muc.text: Risk three: too much permission. You only need it to read your calendar, but you gave it permission to delete your whole inbox.

muc.title: Three safe habits
muc.text: Three habits to stay safe. Only install official servers, or ones already in your app's connector list. Give only the access it needs, called least privilege. And read carefully every time AI asks to do something sensitive, like sending, deleting or paying.

muc.title: Clean up your sockets
muc.text: Open your connector list and remove the ones you no longer use. For the rest, if there's an option to always ask first, turn it on.

muc.title: What about many AIs?
muc.text: One AI with many tools is already powerful. So what about many AIs working together, called multi-agent? Part five.
